evidence: Structural wiring verified by parsing the frozen bytes with tomllib and by diffing against the frozen template. (1) tests/scoring.toml:1-11 is byte-identical to the template: [gates] render=0.0, constraints=0.0; [weights] functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2 (positive, sum 1); [floors] functional=0.05 (a weighted dimension). Directories tests/gates/{render,constraints} and tests/scored/{functional,polish,visual} exist, each with judge.toml + prompt.md; no reward.toml or stray tests/ entries. (2) All five judge.toml [judge] headers are identical to the template headers (diff of everything up to the first [[criterion]]): judge='claude-code', mode='batched', isolated=false, prompt_template='prompt.md'; no model/reasoning_effort/temperature/weight keys. Timeouts: render 600, constraints 600, functional 9000, polish 900, visual 900. (3) Every judge.toml declares [[judge.mcp_servers]] name='playwright', command 'playwright-mcp', args ['--headless','--isolated','--executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium','--no-sandbox']. Only scored/functional/judge.toml:14-18 adds name='verifier', command '/usr/local/bin/python3', args ['/tests/tools/restart_mcp.py', '$APP_RESTART_HELPER']; test.sh:127-193 generates app-restart.sh by heredoc + sed, chmod 755, removes the .used marker and `export APP_RESTART_HELPER="$LOG_DIR/app-restart.sh"` before run_suite gates/scored (test.sh:203-227); restart_mcp.py:9 reads sys.argv[1], exposes the single tool 'restart_app' (line 14) that is single-use via a '.used' marker (lines 29-31). test.sh, score.py and restart_mcp.py are byte-identical to the template. The functional prompt (prompt.md:1, :51) names restart_app, limits it to protocol D, and says 'No shell'; no other prompt mentions restarting. (4) Criteria: gates/render 1 binary (hro_gate_render, weight 1.0), gates/constraints 1 binary (hro_gate_shared, weight 1.0), both aggregation='all_pass' -> gates binary. scored/functional 43 binary, unique ids, positive weights (sum 58.5), non-empty descriptions, aggregation='weighted_mean'. scored/polish 5 binary, unique, positive weights (sum 12.0), weighted_mean. scored/visual 5 likert with points=5 and 5 described anchors each, weight 1.2 each, weighted_mean. name==id everywhere. (5) Prompts resolve: each prompt.md contains exactly the placeholders {app_context} and {criteria} and no other brace characters (grep for [{}] outside those two lines returns nothing; judge.toml files contain no braces either), so neither test.sh's {app_context} substitution (test.sh:195-201, glob /tests/*/*/prompt.md covers all five) nor RewardKit's {criteria} substitution can hit a stray placeholder; app_context.md is non-empty (1617 chars) with Application/Accounts/Key screens. Each prompt opens http://localhost:3000 and carries the untrusted-submission line. (6) Gate semantics in score.py: gates_passed = all(score > 0.0); an all_pass binary gate yields 0 or 1, so a gate failure is exit 1 (detailed record kept) and the scored suite is skipped. (7) Budget nesting: gate judges 600+600=1200 < gate suite 1500; with --max-concurrent-agent 1 scored judges 9000+900+900=10800 < scored suite 11100; 1500+11100=12600 < [verifier].timeout_sec 13200 (task.toml). Adversarial probes: a broken app cannot exploit the wiring — weights/floors/gates live only in scoring.toml and score.py is canonical; a static shell fails both binary all_pass gates and score.py zeroes the reward. A conforming alternative app is not disadvantaged structurally: the restart tool is wired exactly as the canonical template and no prompt requires a route, file or shell.
